folio_note: 9 letters. EMLO says the numeric cipher words are not decoded in SP 29/169 f. 155 (31 Aug) and SP 29/172 f. 15 (17 Sept, to Killigrew); others are decoded interlinear; SP 29/169 f. 47 postscript gives the key to her symbol cipher.

title: Comenius → Andreas Klobusiczky, cipher passage of 24 May 1655 (Rákóczi archive)
correspondents: Jan Amos Komenský (Comenius) → Andreas Klobusiczky (Rákóczi's councillor)
shelfmark: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár Országos Levéltár (Budapest), E 190 (Archivum familiae Rákóczi): 5.t. 788 ff. 389-390v; 6962 ff. 351-354v; 5.t. 800 ff. 414-415v
folio_note: One passage of 50 letters and the numbers 7, 865, 73 inside news quoted from an English correspondent; printed MHH XXIII (1874) no. CIII p. 178 and Patera 1892 no. CLII p. 178 (italic). The 4 Aug 1655 sentence is deciphered (write-up comenius1655); 22 Jul and 6 Sept have invisible ink / secret script printed in clear by Szilágyi 1890.
status: 4 Aug 1655 sentence deciphered in print (Szilágyi 1890 p. 393; Patera 1892 p. 182); key = Rákóczi envoys' table, MHH XXIII p. 740. The 24 May passage does not decipher with that table, shifts, keyword ciphers, or as a simple substitution of Latin (annealing with matched control); no decipherment in MHH, Szilágyi 1890 or Patera. See targets/comenius1655/.
why: Comenius's secret line to George II Rákóczi on the Swedish-Polish war of 1655, when he pressed Transylvania to join Sweden.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 EMLO sweep (research/founders_emlo/); not viewed
verify: Needs the original (MNL OL E 190) for the readings (Xyopatus / Xyoapus, long s / f) and any key; the cipher may belong to the English correspondent.

frame_check.frame: APUG 563 f. 179v and f. 181r (crops on the Wuerzburg page, images botschaft_1a.jpg and botschaft_2.jpg)
frame_check.saw: Not the Gregorian repository viewer (EMLO page never loaded; archimede.imss.fi.it/kircher/563/large/ is 403 and the Stanford Luna Insight route is obsolete). I saw two crops of the cryptogram leaves reproduced by Vollrath (Wuerzburg), captioned Ausschnitte aus APUG 563 179v und 181r. 179v: a circle containing a 12x12 grid of the numbers 1-144 in scrambled order (41 80 11 74 12 90 ...), with a 4-line Latin instruction above in Kirchers hand (in quadrato hoc numeros continens ... ). 181r: a circle with a 12x12 grid of Latin syllables (vo tus sint ri prin quan to lu ...), a Latin note above (Jam hic secreta ex praecedenti tabula ...) and a tally of strokes with the number 35. So the cryptogram is a numbered square plus a syllable square, a key-and-message pair, in Latin. No decipherment written on them.
frame_check.note: Page text says the enigma was Kirchers own, sent to the duke, with the dukes receipt dated 29 Sept 1664 answering a letter of 31 Aug; so the cryptogram leaves ff.179-181 look like Kirchers enigma rather than a dukes cryptogram, and the 1 Jun 1664 letter ff.88r-89v was not viewed. Whole leaves not seen, only crops.
